sights.n: Sakai Traditional Crafts Museum (Sakai Densho-kan) — Sakai knives
sights.w: Showcase and shop for Sakai's 600-year knife-forging tradition (plus incense, tea and textiles), with live sharpening demos — Sakai is one of Japan's three great cutlery towns.

sights.n: Sakai Plaza of Rikyū and Akiko (Sakai Rishō no Mori)
sights.address: Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka (facing the site of Sen no Rikyū's residence)
sights.w: 2015 museum on Sakai's two icons — tea master Sen no Rikyū and poet Yosano Akiko — with a standing-style (ryūrei) tea service and a tea room facing Rikyū's old house site.

sights.n: Nisanzai Kofun (土師ニサンザイ古墳)
sights.w: One of the largest keyhole tombs of the UNESCO Mozu-Furuichi group (late 5th c.), its moat-ringed mound a quieter, more photogenic alternative to Nintoku's tomb.
Early-Meiji public park and pine grove on the old western approach to Sumiyoshi Taisha, beside Nankai Sumiyoshi-kōen Station.
